full.description: This is a micrograph showing a cerebrospinal fluid sample stained with mucicarmine. The image reveals numerous encapsulated yeast-like cells dispersed within the specimen. These encapsulated structures are characteristic of Cryptococcus species. The most likely diagnosis is cryptococcosis, often observed in cerebrospinal fluid examination.

blind.description: This is a microscopic image of a tissue section showing an epithelial element composed of ducts, acini, tubules, sheets, and strands of cuboidal and myoepithelial cells. The surrounding stroma exhibits features typical of benign or proliferative breast pathology. The overall appearance is consistent with a benign breast lesion such as fibroadenoma or ductal hyperplasia.

random.description: This is a microscopic view of tissue stained with a special stain highlighting calcified deposits and hemosiderin. The image shows Gamna-Gandy bodies, which are characterized by yellow-brown nodules of fibrous tissue containing iron and calcium deposits. These lesions are typically found in the red pulp of the spleen in conditions such as portal hypertension or sickle cell anemia. The presence of these distinctive bodies confirms the diagnosis of Gamna-Gandy bodies (siderotic nodules) in the splenic tissue.
